disposition_reason: CBI export-market guidance (last updated 10 July 2024) restates the four EU cocoa/chocolate Cd MLs in Table 2 (mg/kg wet weight) and reports buyer practice: some buyers reject beans above 0.3 mg/kg Cd, and 0.3 mg/kg beans yield cake/powder at about 0.6 mg/kg.
disposition_locator: Section 1 'Heavy metals, specifically cadmium', Table 2 and text above it (PDF p. 6)

study.material_scope: secondary restatement of EU cocoa Cd MLs; buyer bean acceptance thresholds

controls.control: Buyer acceptance threshold: some buyers reject cocoa beans exceeding 0.3 mg/kg Cd, especially for cocoa powder production
controls.outcome: bean Cd 0.3 mg/kg -> cake/powder about 0.6 mg/kg (stated concentration ratio ~2x)

controls.control: Blend beans to lower overall Cd; test peeled beans (shell Cd higher than nib)
Liming and organic amendments (compost, biochar) to reduce plant Cd uptake; low-Cd varieties via breeding or grafting

regulatory.product: Milk chocolate with less than 30% of total dry cocoa solids
Chocolate with less than 50% of total dry cocoa solids; milk chocolate with 30% or more of total dry cocoa solids
Chocolate with 50% or more of total dry cocoa solids
Cocoa powder sold to the final consumer or as an ingredient in sweetened cocoa powder sold to the final consumer (drinking chocolate)

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Text says a 'maximum level of 0.6 or 0.8 mg per kilogram of peeled cocoa beans may be safe'; EU law sets no ML for cocoa beans. This is CBI commentary, not a legal limit.
Text describes Reg. (EU) 2023/915 as 'on the maximum levels of cadmium in certain food products'; it covers all listed contaminants.
unresolved: Document predates Reg. (EU) 2024/1987 (nickel) and does not mention it.
